attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his own newsletter essay. He presents it as his assertion, not a quote of someone else.

semantics.note: Captures the core 'cannot afford' claim and links the NVIDIA money to data-center deployment. It leaves out the side assertion that NVIDIA 'hasn't sent a cent', though the contract keeps it as a source element. Reading it as a present-tense observation of capacity is reasonable.

contract.note: Reading 'afford' as the ability to pay when due, including credible financing, is a fair, ordinary reading of firm language ('most assuredly'). It does not require the full headline amount in cash. The result depends on matching payment schedules to financing, and the packet lacks that.

evidence.note: OpenAI's own disclosure describes a multiyear Oracle partnership over $300B. It gives no payment schedule and does not establish affordability either way.
Joint company letter of intent: NVIDIA's investment comes progressively as capacity is deployed. It describes the structure only and does not show funding capacity or whether any payment was made.

CNBC: leasing spreads GPU costs, and an initial $10B will be 'available soon'. This weakens a simple upfront-cash comparison, but the report says costs and timing are undetermined, so it settles neither side.
Unverified estimate, relayed second-hand, of about $17.5B cash at mid-2025. It covers a different date and a narrower measure than financing capacity, so it is context only.

reviews.rationale: The contract needs dated payment obligations matched against liquidity and committed financing as of publication. The packet has company announcements, a leasing report and an earlier unverified cash estimate, but no payment schedule and no record of financing available on that date. It neither shows an unavoidable shortfall nor proves the resources were sufficient. Nothing in it shows whether NVIDIA had paid anything by then.
